title: Round record contract
description: One JSON line per round of the method, appended to state/round-record.jsonl. The rubric_hash ties the round to the frozen sha256 of the 'Rubric' section the verdict applied to; the verdict enum mirrors the mechanical rule of that section (rejected, accepted, accepted with conditions); rubric_author names who wrote that rubric.

method_version.description: Semantic version of the method this round ran under.

model.description: The executor of the role, by family (a letter kept stable across the material, e.g. 'family A') and effort, never by model identifier: a product identifier changes and leaks the provider, and the family is what the rule of independence uses. The map from letter to identifier stays with the owner, outside the material. A route or alias is not a family: two executors differ when what their names map to differs. Since v0.5.0 a reviewer is described by its relation to the producer ('reviewer, same family as the producer' or 'reviewer, another family'), never as 'independent' when the family is the same; the lines written before are never rewritten.

tokens.description: Since v0.6.0, optional: the tokens the role used in the round, from the usage the endpoint returned.

calls.description: Since v0.6.0, optional: the calls the role made.

finish.description: Since v0.6.0, optional: how the generation of the role's last call ended (stop, length, error); a length is a tool failure, never a result.

summary.description: What the round did, one line.

rubric_author.description: Who wrote the rubric the round applies: a role name, or 'producer', 'reviewer side' or 'owner'. Step 8 of the recipe gives the rubric to the owner and the reviewing side; a rubric written by the producer is recorded as such, never left implicit. Since the rework of v0.6.0 a chained line with 'rubric_applied' true and 'rubric_author' 'producer' is a low note of the validator ('rubric written by the producer').

family_map_commitment.description: Since the rework of v0.6.0, required on a chained line of method_version 0.6.0 or later: a salted commitment to the map from the letters the lines use (family A, B, ...) to the families they stand for. Canonical form: the sha256, over UTF-8, of json.dumps(map, sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ':'), ensure_ascii=False) + '\n' + salt, where map is the object letter -> description of the family and salt a string of 64 hex characters the owner keeps. The map and the salt stay with the owner, outside the material; the validator checks the form (64 hex) only, and the owner proves the commitment by revealing both. It lets a later reader check that the letters were not reassigned after the fact, without the material naming any family.

prev.description: Since v0.6.0: the sha256 of every line above this one, each followed by LF (for a file with no blank line, the sha256 of the file before the line was appended). The validator recomputes the chain: an earlier line edited, removed or reordered breaks it. Lines written before the chain carry none; the canon's 'Chained ledgers' table says how many.

kind.description: Since v0.6.0, required on a chained line: a production runs the method on a target (brief, rubric on the reviewing side, stop); a maintenance round corrects the material and emits no verdict of the canon.

reviewer_relation.description: Since v0.6.0, required on a chained line with a reviewer role: the reviewer's relation to the producer.

rubric_applied.description: Since v0.6.0: true when the round's review applied the frozen rubric; the validator then compares rubric_hash with the sha256 of the frozen rubric. A rubric_hash on a line without it records the pin in force, not that it was applied.

rounds_to_stop.description: Since v0.6.0, optional: the rounds the target took until its stopping criterion (a production).

wall_seconds.description: Since v0.6.0, optional: the wall time of the round, beside the throughput of the same run when it is compared.

notes_count.description: Since v0.6.0, optional: the notes the round's review and validator emitted.

crew.description: Since v0.6.0, optional: the roles that ran in the round.
